transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you lately that brought you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brought me in is that I've been having this issue late at night. What really worries me is that once I start picking at food, I just can't seem to stop. I literally tell myself, that is enough, Santiago, but my hand just keeps going back for more. It is honestly like I don't get to make the decision anymore. It just keeps happening, and that's what has been troubling me.
Can you describe what typically happens during these episodes? For example, do you feel a strong compulsion or urge to keep eating even when you’re not hungry?

Yeah, that's exactly it. I mean, a lot of times I'm not even hungry. I'll have already eaten dinner with the rest of the family, so I know I'm full. But then later on, I still end up opening the fridge and just... starting all over again. It's like the hunger doesn't even matter.
Do you feel like you're not in control once you start eating, like you can't stop even if you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly how it feels. Like I said earlier, once I start picking at the food late at night, I just can't stop. I'll literally tell myself, "That's enough, Santiago," but my hand just keeps going back for more. It really is like I don't get to make the decision anymore once I start. I just lose all control.
Has this behavior been causing you any distress or affecting your daily life in any way?

It hasn't really affected my work. I’m still getting to my shipping and receiving shifts and handling all my responsibilities there just fine. But at home... I guess it is causing some issues. 

I’ve actually started avoiding some of our late family time if people are hanging out in the kitchen. I just, um... I'm worried someone is going to notice how uneasy I am around the food. So I just kind of stay away instead.
When you’re late at night and you start eating, do you keep going until there’s no more food left?

Yeah, pretty much. I mean, on some of those nights after work, I can go through a lot. I'll eat several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left over from dinner. I just stand there in the kitchen eating it all, almost like I'm just cleaning up the leftovers, but I'm really just eating until it's gone.
When you’re eating during these late-night episodes, do you find yourself eating much faster than usual or until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yeah, I do eat pretty fast during those times. It's not like when I'm sitting down with the family and just taking my time. It's more like... I'm trying to get it all done before anyone wakes up. I eat so quick I barely even taste the food. And yeah, by the time the food is gone, I definitely feel uncomfortably full.
Do these late-night eating episodes make you feel ashamed or upset with yourself afterward?

Yeah, I do. I mean, once I'm done and I'm standing there looking at the empty pots... I just feel really bad about it. I feel guilty, like I shouldn't have done it, and I definitely feel ashamed. It's just... it's a pretty lousy feeling to have right before you try to go to sleep.
Doctor: Are you fully awake and aware during these late-night eating episodes, or do you find yourself eating while still partially asleep?
No, I'm fully awake. I mean, I don't sleepwalk or anything like that. I'm definitely conscious of what I'm doing when I'm in the kitchen... I just can't seem to stop myself once I start.
Do you usually eat until there's no more food available, even if you're already feeling full?

No, not really. I mean, I don't eat until the house is completely out of food. There's always stuff left in the pantry or the fridge. I usually just stop when... well, when I hit that point where I'm just too stuffed and uncomfortable to keep going, or when the specific thing I was eating is finished. I don't just keep hunting for every last thing we have.
Has this eating behavior caused you significant distress or impaired your functioning in social, occupational, or other important areas of life?

Well, as far as work goes, no. I mean, I'm still getting to my shipping and receiving shifts on time and handling all my responsibilities there just fine. It hasn't messed with my job or anything like that. 

But... I guess it is affecting things at home a little bit. I've actually started avoiding some of our late family time if everyone's hanging out in the kitchen. I just... I get worried someone is going to notice how uneasy I am around the food. So it's just easier for me to steer clear and go to another room.
Can you recall if this sense of not being able to stop eating once you start happens during times other than late at night, or is it mostly just at night when this occurs?

It's pretty much just at night. During the day... well, I don't really have that problem. If I'm on my shift or just eating a regular lunch or dinner, I can eat a normal amount and just stop when I'm done. I haven't really noticed that feeling of not being able to stop at any other time besides late in the evening.
Do these late-night eating episodes usually happen after something stressful or upsetting has occurred during your day, or do they seem to happen more randomly?

Well, I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. It doesn't seem to matter if I had a bad day at work or if everything was just totally fine. I mean, I guess it feels pretty random. I'll just be sitting there watching TV or whatever, and the urge just hits me, regardless of how the day went.
Even if it doesn't seem connected to a stressful day, do these late-night eating episodes usually happen when you're feeling a certain way, like bored, sad, or anxious?

Honestly, I'm not really sure. I haven't noticed any specific feeling attached to it. I don't think I'm particularly sad or anxious when it happens. I guess maybe I could be a little bored, just sitting around watching TV, but it doesn't really stand out as a strong emotion or anything. It just... happens.
Do these late-night eating episodes ever start when you're feeling down, stressed, or anxious, or do they seem to come out of nowhere emotionally?
Like I said, I really haven't noticed any connection to my mood. It doesn't seem to matter if I'm stressed or down or anything like that. It just kind of comes out of nowhere, emotionally speaking.
During these late-night eating episodes, are you usually not hungry at all when you start eating?

Yeah, a lot of times I'm not even hungry. I mean, I usually eat dinner with everybody else, so I'm full from that. But then later on, I still just end up opening the fridge and starting all over again.
